title.deva: मोहब्बत करने वाले कम न होंगे

intro: This ghazal by Hafeez Hoshiarpuri explores themes of unfulfilled love, longing, and separation. The poet reflects on the idea that while there may be many admirers of the beloved, he himself will not be among them. He contrasts the weight of personal sorrow against the world’s collective grief, suggesting that the pain of loving and losing the beloved surpasses all other troubles. Despite the possibility of reunion, the scars of separation remain, making love a bittersweet experience. The poem captures heartbreak, quiet acceptance, and the melancholic fate of the unrequited lover.

deva: मोहब्बत करने वाले कम न होंगे
तिरी महफ़िल में लेकिन हम न होंगे

en: There will be no shortage of those who love you,
But in your gathering, I will not be present.

deva: मैं अक्सर सोचता हूँ फूल कब तक

en: I often wonder, how long will flowers
Continue to share the tears of the dewdrop?

gloss.meaning: partners in the weeping of the dew

deva: सितम ही इश्क़ में पैहम न होंगे

en: Yet love is not always filled with suffering.

gloss.meaning: slow to warm, late to recognise

deva: अगर कुछ मशवरे बाहम न होंगे

en: The confusions of hearts will only grow,
If lovers do not share their counsel.

deva: ज़माने भर के ग़म या इक तिरा ग़म
ये ग़म होगा तो कितने ग़म न होंगे

en: The grief of the entire world or just your sorrow:
If your pain exists, what other pains could remain?

deva: वो मेरे हाल से महरम न होंगे

en: Why should I call the people of the world heartless?
They are simply unaware of my condition.
My heart will be flooded with tears,
If my eyes do not carry their usual sorrow.

deva: अगर तू इत्तिफ़ाक़न मिल भी जाए
तिरी फ़ुर्क़त के सदमे कम न होंगे

en: Even if by some chance I meet you,
The pain of separation will never diminish.

deva: 'हफ़ीज़' उन से मैं जितना बद-गुमाँ हूँ
वो मुझ से उस क़दर बरहम न होंगे

en: Hafeez, no matter how much I distrust them,
They will never be as displeased with me as I am with them.

gloss.meaning: the poet’s pen name, signed into the last couplet

listing.summary: There will be no shortage of those who love you, but I will not be among them. A ghazal of separation whose sorrow, the poet suggests, outweighs the grief of the whole world.
